description: In Elixir, def f(_s, limit, limit) matches only when the 2nd and 3rd arguments are equal. fz ignores the repetition: with def f(_s, limit, limit), do: :same and def f(_s, _l, _a), do: :different, M.f(:x, 1, 2) returns :same (Elixir: :different), and fz warns type/redundant-clause that the second clause is unreachable. Silent wrong answer, reproduced on ad21e1635. Found by the fz-sc8.14 builder. A repeated pattern variable must bind once and compare (===) at every other occurrence, in function heads, case and receive patterns, and = matches, on all three paths, with the decision tree and redundancy check seeing the equality.
title: A variable repeated in a function head matches only equal arguments
